senses.en: Scarcity; a lack or short supply.

examples.text: A dearth of signalmen and the high cost of labour is hastening an elimination process that already was well under way before the second world war.

origin.ko: dear(귀한)에 -th가 붙은 말입니다. 물건이 귀해지는 것, 곧 '부족'을 뜻하게 되었습니다.

senses.en: a sudden and violent collapse

examples.text: The merger turned into a financial debacle that cost thousands of employees their jobs.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 débâcler(빗장을 풀다)에서 왔습니다. 막아둔 것이 풀려 쏟아지듯 '총체적 붕괴'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: To lower in character, quality, or value; to degrade.

examples.text: Critics argued that constant sensationalism had debased the quality of public debate on television.

senses.en: To lower the value of (a currency) by reducing the amount of valuable metal in the coins.
senses.ko: (화폐의) 품위를 낮추다, 질 낮은 금속을 섞다

examples.text: Roman emperors repeatedly debased the silver denarius to pay for their costly military campaigns.

origin.ko: de-와 base(낮은)를 합친 말입니다. 질을 낮은 쪽으로 끌어내린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: impairing the strength and vitality

examples.text: She suffered from a debilitating illness that left her too weak to climb stairs.

senses.en: having a sophisticated charm

examples.text: The debonair host greeted each guest by name and kept every conversation effortlessly alive.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 de bon aire '좋은 혈통의'에서 왔습니다. 품위 있는 사람의 태도가 '세련된'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: To discredit, or expose to ridicule the falsehood or the exaggerated claims of something; to refute.

examples.text: The physicist debunked the psychic's claims

origin.ko: de-(제거)에 bunk(헛소리)를 합친 1923년의 말입니다. 헛소리를 걷어내니 '허위를 폭로하다'입니다.

senses.en: A young woman who makes her first formal appearance in society.

examples.text: The debutante curtsied to the guests at the ball her family had hosted in her honor.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 débutante에서 왔고 debut(첫 등장)에 -ante가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: the state of being degenerate in mental or moral qualities

examples.text: Historians often cite the decadence of the late empire as a cause of its eventual fall.

senses.en: With a positive connotation: the quality of being luxuriously enjoyable or self-indulgent, especially of food; luxuriousness, richness.

examples.text: the decadence of a five-star hotel

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 decadentia에서 왔고 '아래로 떨어짐'이 어원입니다. 쇠퇴하는 상태가 '퇴폐'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: marked by excessive self-indulgence and moral decay

examples.text: a decadent life of excessive money and no sense of responsibility

senses.en: luxuriously self-indulgent

examples.text: I spent a decadent day at a spa

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēcadere(아래로 떨어지다)에서 왔습니다. 몰락해 가는 상태를 가리킵니다.

senses.en: The killing or destruction of any large portion of a population.

examples.text: The plague caused the decimation of villages across the valley within a single winter.

origin.ko: 라틴어 decimātiō에서 왔습니다. 로마군이 열 명 중 한 명을 처형한 벌에서 '대량 살상'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: To read text that is almost illegible or obscure.

examples.text: The archivist spent weeks trying to decipher the faded handwriting in the soldier's letters.

senses.en: To convert a code or cipher to plain text.

examples.text: Wartime analysts worked around the clock to decipher the enemy's intercepted radio messages.

origin.ko: de-와 cipher(암호)를 합친 말입니다. 암호를 풀어 '판독하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: speak against in an impassioned manner

examples.text: he declaimed against the wasteful ways of modern society

senses.en: recite in elocution

examples.text: The actor declaimed the famous soliloquy to a hushed and attentive theater.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēclāmō(큰 소리로 연설하다)에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: a downward slope or bend

examples.text: The path followed a steep declivity into the valley, where a stream wound between the trees.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēclīvis(아래로 기운)에서 왔고 clīvus(비탈)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: characterized by propriety and dignity and good taste in manners and conduct

examples.text: The guests maintained a decorous silence throughout the long and solemn ceremony.

origin.ko: 라틴어 decōrus(어울리는, 알맞은)에서 왔고 decor(품위)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: propriety in manners and conduct

examples.text: The judge demanded decorum in the courtroom and warned the spectators against further outbursts.

origin.ko: 라틴어 decōrum(어울리는 것)에서 왔습니다. 상황에 맞는 행동이 '예의'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: An edict or law.

examples.text: The king issued a decree banning all public gatherings after the riots.

senses.en: decide with authority

examples.text: The King decreed that all firstborn males should be killed

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēcrētum(결정된 것)에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다.

senses.en: express strong disapproval of

examples.text: Environmental groups decried the decision to open the protected wetlands to commercial development.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 descrier(소리치다)에서 왔습니다. 외쳐서 가치를 깎아내리는 뜻으로 발전했습니다.

senses.en: To reach (a conclusion) by applying rules of logic or other forms of reasoning to given premises or known facts.

examples.text: From the muddy footprints, the detective deduced that the intruder had entered through the garden.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēdūcere(끌어내다)에서 왔습니다. 전제에서 결론을 끌어내니 '추론하다'입니다.

senses.en: To hold in belief or estimation; to adjudge as a conclusion; to regard as being; to evaluate according to one's beliefs; to account.

examples.text: She deemed his efforts insufficient.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 dēman(판단하다, 선고하다)에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: mar or spoil the appearance of

examples.text: Vandals defaced the memorial overnight, spraying slogans across its marble base.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 desfacier(훼손하다)에서 왔습니다. 얼굴(face)을 지워 버린다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: To fail to fulfill a financial obligation.

examples.text: to default on a loan

senses.en: A selection made in the absence of an alternative.

examples.text: With no other candidate willing to run, she won the chairmanship by default.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 defaute(결함, 부족)에서 왔고, 라틴어 fallo(속이다)와 이어집니다. 채무를 못 갚는 '불이행'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Great respect.

examples.text: The children treated their elders with deference.

senses.en: a disposition or tendency to yield to the will of others

examples.text: The young associate showed such deference to the partners that she rarely voiced her own opinions.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 déférence에서 왔고 defer(따르다)에 -ence가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: Respectful and considerate; showing deference.

examples.text: The deferential intern spoke only when invited and thanked everyone for their time.

origin.ko: deference에 -al이 붙은 말로, 월터 스콧이 만들었다고 합니다.

senses.en: To make (something) deviate from its original path or position.

examples.text: A thin metal shield deflected the blast away from the control room.

senses.en: To avoid addressing (questions, criticism, etc.).

examples.text: The Prime Minister deflected some increasingly pointed questions by claiming he had an appointment.

origin.ko: 라틴어 deflectō에서 왔습니다. 가던 길에서 휘어 벗어나게 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To pay or discharge (a debt, expense etc.); to meet (the cost of something).

examples.text: A small grant from the foundation helped defray the cost of the students' research trip.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 défrayer에서 왔고 고대 프랑스어 fraier(쓰다)와 이어집니다. 비용을 대신 쓴다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: skillful in physical movements; especially of the hands

examples.text: With a few deft strokes of the brush, the artist captured the old man's weary expression.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 dæfte(온화한, 알맞은)에서 왔습니다. '적절한'에서 '솜씨 좋은'으로 의미가 이동했습니다.

senses.en: To lower in value or social position.

examples.text: Fred degrades himself by his behaviour.

senses.en: To reduce in quality or purity.

examples.text: The DNA sample has degraded.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 dégrader에서 왔습니다. 단계를 아래로 내린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To regard as being like a deity; to treat as worthy of worship; to exalt.

examples.text: Admirers deified the founder, treating his every casual remark as sacred wisdom.

origin.ko: 라틴어 deus(신)에서 deificāre를 거쳐 왔습니다. 신으로 만든다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: do something that one considers to be below one's dignity

examples.text: He didn’t even deign to give us a nod of the head; he thought us that far beneath him.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dignāre(~할 만하다고 여기다)에서 왔습니다. 자기 품위에 맞는다고 여겨 '황송하게 ~해 주다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: lower someone's spirits; make downhearted

examples.text: The team's third straight loss dejected the players and silenced the locker room.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēicere(아래로 던지다)에서 왔습니다. 기분을 아래로 내던지니 '낙담시키다'입니다.

senses.en: To commit (a task or responsibility) to someone, especially a subordinate.

examples.text: A good manager learns to delegate routine tasks so that she can focus on strategy.

senses.en: A person authorized to act as representative for another; a deputy.

examples.text: Each state sent a delegate to the convention to vote on the proposed treaty.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēlēgāre(보내다, 맡기다)에서 왔습니다. 일을 맡겨 보내는 데서 '위임하다'입니다.

senses.en: Harmful, often in a subtle or unexpected way.

examples.text: deleterious to someone's health

origin.ko: 그리스어 dēlētḗrios(해로운)에서 왔습니다. 'delete'와는 관련이 없습니다.

senses.en: characterized by conscious design or purpose

examples.text: a deliberate attempt to cover up his crime

senses.en: unhurried and with care and dignity

examples.text: with all deliberate speed

senses.en: think about carefully; weigh

examples.text: The jury deliberated for two days before reaching a unanimous verdict.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēlīberāre(저울질하다)에서 왔습니다. 저울에 달 듯 따져보고 한 일이라 '고의적인'입니다.

senses.en: Tact and propriety; the need for such tact.

examples.text: The ambassador handled the diplomatic crisis with great delicacy, avoiding any word that might offend.

senses.en: Something appealing, usually a pleasing food, especially a choice dish of a certain culture suggesting rarity and refinement.

examples.text: a Chinese delicacy

senses.en: Frailty of health or fitness.

examples.text: The delicacy of the premature infant's lungs required constant monitoring in the hospital.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 delicat(섬세한)에서 왔고 delicate에 -acy가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: set, mark, or draw the boundaries of something

examples.text: The treaty delimited the border between the two nations along the course of the river.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 dēlīmitō(경계를 표시하다)에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: show the form or outline of

examples.text: The sketch delineated the building's silhouette against the evening sky with a few bold lines.

senses.en: describe in vivid detail

examples.text: The report delineates the responsibilities of each department so that no duties are overlooked.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēlīneāre(선으로 그려내다)에서 왔습니다. 선으로 윤곽을 그려 보인다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a mistaken or unfounded opinion or idea

examples.text: he has delusions of competence

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēlūsiō(속임)에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: To search thoroughly and carefully for information, research, dig into, penetrate, fathom, trace out

examples.text: The biographer delved into decades of letters to understand the poet's troubled final years.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 delfan(땅을 파다)에서 왔습니다. 땅을 파듯 깊이 파고든다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: a political leader who seeks support by appealing to popular passions and prejudices

examples.text: The demagogue stoked fears about immigrants to win votes rather than offering any workable policy.

origin.ko: 그리스어 dēmagōgós '민중의 지도자'에서 왔습니다. 민중을 이끄는 사람이 '선동가'로 변했습니다.

senses.en: set, mark, or draw the boundaries of something

examples.text: Low stone walls demarcate the monastery's land from the neighboring farms.

origin.ko: demarcation에서 만들어진 말입니다. 경계를 표시한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: reduce in worth or character, usually verbally

examples.text: A good teacher never demeans a student for asking a question, however basic it may seem.

origin.ko: de-와 mean(천한)을 합친 1595년의 말입니다. 품위를 낮은 데로 끌어내린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: capable of being demonstrated or proved

examples.text: It is easily demonstrable that water extinguishes fire.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어에서 왔고 라틴어 mōnstrāre(보여주다)가 뿌리입니다. 보여줄 수 있어 '입증 가능한'입니다.

senses.en: given to or marked by the open expression of emotion

examples.text: an affectionate and demonstrative family

senses.en: serving to demonstrate

examples.text: demonstrative evidence

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēmōnstrātīvus에서 왔습니다. 감정을 겉으로 드러내 보인다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To destroy the morale of; to dishearten.

examples.text: Constant layoffs and unclear leadership demoralized the staff and drove the best engineers away.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 démoraliser에서 왔습니다. 사기(morale)를 없앤다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Chiefly followed by to, and sometimes by at or on: to object or be reluctant; to balk, to take exception.

examples.text: The personnel demurred at the management’s new scheme.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēmorārī(지체하다)에서 왔습니다. 선뜻 응하지 않고 미적대다가 '이의를 제기하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: Modest, quiet, reserved, or serious.

examples.text: She is a demure young lady.

senses.en: affectedly modest or shy especially in a playful or provocative way

examples.text: Behind her demure smile lay a sharp wit that she deployed only when the moment was right.

origin.ko: 앵글로노르만어 de mure port '성숙한 태도로'에서 왔다고 봅니다. 차분하고 얌전한 태도를 가리킵니다.

senses.en: To criticize so as to besmirch; traduce, disparage or defame.

examples.text: Rival candidates tried to denigrate her record by distorting her votes on key bills.

senses.en: To treat as worthless; belittle, degrade or disparage.

examples.text: You have no right to denigrate people and things that you have no personal experience with.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēnigrāre(검게 칠하다)에서 왔습니다. 남을 검게 칠해 평판을 더럽힌다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: be a sign or indication of

examples.text: The yellow blazes denote the trail.

senses.en: have as a meaning

examples.text: The prefix pre- denotes "before", as in preview.

origin.ko: 라틴어 denotare(표시하다)에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: the final resolution of the main complication of a literary or dramatic work

examples.text: The film's denouement ties up every loose thread, revealing who was behind the theft.

senses.en: the outcome of a complex sequence of events

examples.text: The denouement of the long negotiations surprised even the diplomats who had arranged them.

senses.en: to accuse or condemn or openly or formally or brand as disgraceful

examples.text: He denounced the government action

senses.en: To announce the termination of; especially a treaty or armistice.

examples.text: The new government threatened to denounce the trade agreement unless its terms were renegotiated.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēnūntiō(알리다, 위협하다)에서 왔고 nūntius(전령)가 뿌리입니다. 공공연히 알리며 규탄하는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: slow to learn or understand; lacking intellectual acuity

examples.text: so dense he never understands anything I say to him

senses.en: Obscure or difficult to understand.

examples.text: The philosopher's dense prose rewards patient readers but baffles anyone looking for a quick summary.

senses.en: having component parts closely crowded together

examples.text: a dense population

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēnsus(빽빽한)에서 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 빽빽해서 뚫고 들어가기 어려운 이미지가 '우둔한'으로 이어졌습니다.

senses.en: Bearing; manner of presenting oneself.

examples.text: Her deportment impressed her interviewers.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 déportement에서 왔고 deport(처신하다)에 -ment가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: To remove (a leader) from (high) office without killing (them).

examples.text: A deposed monarch may go into exile as pretender to the lost throne, hoping to be restored in a subsequent revolution.

senses.en: make a deposition; declare under oath

examples.text: The engineer was deposed by the plaintiff's lawyers three months before the trial began.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 deposer에서 왔습니다. 높은 자리에서 아래로 내려놓으니 '폐위하다'입니다.

senses.en: corrupt morally or by intemperance or sensuality

examples.text: Moralists feared that cheap novels would deprave the young and undermine social order.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēprāvāre(비틀다, 타락시키다)에서 왔고 pravus(비뚤어진)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: moral perversion; impairment of virtue and moral principles

examples.text: The trial exposed the depravity of a regime that tortured its own citizens.

senses.en: To express disapproval of, protest or plead against.

examples.text: She deprecated any action which might disturb the peace.

senses.en: To belittle, depreciate.

examples.text: He deprecates any praise of his own merits.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēprecor(재앙을 막아 달라고 빌다)에서 왔습니다. 악을 물리쳐 달라 비는 데서 '반대하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: an act of plundering and pillaging and marauding

examples.text: Coastal villages suffered repeated depredations at the hands of pirates throughout the century.

senses.en: (usually plural) a destructive action

examples.text: the depredations of age and disease

origin.ko: 라틴어 depraedatio에서 왔고 praeda(약탈품)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: failing in what duty requires
senses.ko: 직무를 태만히 하는, 책임을 다하지 않는

examples.text: derelict (or delinquent) in his duty

senses.en: forsaken by owner or inhabitants

examples.text: The derelict mill, long since abandoned by its owners, slowly crumbled beside the silent canal.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dērelictus(완전히 버려진)에서 왔습니다. 맡은 의무를 버려둔 상태가 '직무 태만'입니다.

senses.en: To laugh at or mock (someone or something) harshly; to ridicule, to scorn.

examples.text: Critics derided the proposal as naive, but it later became the basis of national policy.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dērīdēre(비웃다)에서 왔습니다. 상대를 깔보며 웃는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: abusing vocally; expressing contempt or ridicule

examples.text: derisive laughter

origin.ko: 라틴어 dērīdeō(비웃다)의 어간에 -ive가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: Imitative of the work of someone else.

examples.text: Reviewers dismissed the novel as derivative, a pale echo of the author's more inventive early work.

senses.en: Obtained by derivation; not radical, original, or fundamental.

examples.text: a derivative word

senses.en: a financial instrument whose value is based on another security

examples.text: Complex derivatives tied to subprime mortgages amplified losses across the global banking system.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dērīvāre(물을 끌어내다)에서 왔습니다. 남의 물줄기에서 가져온 것이라 '모방적인'입니다.

senses.en: To obtain or receive (something) from something else.

examples.text: Reading books is the best way to derive knowledge.

senses.en: To originate or stem (from).

examples.text: Her excellent organisation skills derive from her time as a secretary in the army.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dērīvō '물을 끌어내다'에서 왔고 rīvus(시내)가 뿌리입니다. 물줄기를 끌어오듯 '얻다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: formed or developed from something else; not original

examples.text: The French language is derived from Latin.

origin.ko: derive에 -ed가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: expressive of low opinion

examples.text: derogatory comments

senses.en: To see, especially from afar; to discover (a distant or obscure object) by the eye; to espy; to discern or detect.

examples.text: From the crow's nest, the lookout could just descry a faint line of land on the horizon.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 descrier(외쳐 알리다)에서 왔다고 봅니다. decry와 같은 계열의 이중어입니다.

senses.en: To profane or violate the sacredness or sanctity of something.

examples.text: Vandals desecrated the ancient cemetery, overturning headstones and scrawling slogans across the chapel walls.

origin.ko: de-와 consecrate(봉헌하다)의 어간을 합친 말입니다. 신성함을 벗겨낸다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To remove moisture from; to dry; (sometimes) to dry to an extreme degree.

examples.text: Months of relentless sun and wind desiccated the soil until it crumbled into dust.

senses.en: lacking vitality or spirit; lifeless

examples.text: The pianist gave a technically flawless but desiccate rendering, devoid of any warmth or feeling.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēsiccāre(완전히 말리다)에서 왔고 siccus(마른)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: thoroughly dried out

examples.text: old boxes of desiccated Cuban cigars

senses.en: lacking vitality or spirit; lifeless

examples.text: The professor's desiccated lectures drained all the excitement from what should have been a vivid subject.

senses.en: Something that is wished for, or considered desirable, particularly when thought to be essential.

examples.text: For the committee, transparency was the chief desideratum in any new funding procedure.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēsīderātum '바라던 것'에서 왔습니다. 별(sīdus)에서 왔다는 설이 있지만 불확실합니다.

senses.en: Loss of hope; utter hopelessness; complete despondency.

examples.text: He turned around in despair, aware that he was not going to survive.

senses.en: abandon hope; give up hope; lose heart

examples.text: Don't despair — help is on the way!

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēspērāre(희망을 잃다)에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 희망(esperer)이 없는 상태입니다.

senses.en: To plunder; to pillage; take spoil from.

examples.text: Invading armies despoiled the countryside, carrying off grain, livestock, and church treasures.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēspoliāre에서 왔고 spolium(벗긴 가죽, 전리품)이 뿌리입니다. 빼앗아 벗긴다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: someone who takes spoils or plunder (as in war)

examples.text: The chronicler cursed the despoiler who had stripped the abbey of its gold and manuscripts.

origin.ko: despoil에 -er이 붙어 약탈하는 사람을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: a cruel and oppressive dictator

examples.text: The despot silenced his critics, jailed journalists, and ruled the country for three decades.

origin.ko: 그리스어 despótēs(주인, 주군)에서 왔습니다. 집안의 주인이 절대 권력자인 '폭군'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: characteristic of an absolute ruler or absolute rule; having absolute sovereignty

examples.text: The despotic ruler abolished the parliament and imprisoned anyone who questioned his decrees.

origin.ko: 그리스어 despotikós에서 왔고 despot(절대 군주)에 -ic이 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: poor enough to need help from others

examples.text: The war left thousands of families destitute and dependent on charity for food.

senses.en: completely wanting or lacking

examples.text: young recruits destitute of experience

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēstitūtus(버려진, 남겨진)에서 왔습니다. 의지할 것 없이 내버려진 상태가 '극빈'입니다.

senses.en: marked by lack of definite plan or regularity or purpose; jumping from one thing to another

examples.text: the desultory conversation characteristic of cocktail parties

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēsultor(달리는 말에서 다른 말로 뛰어 옮겨 타는 곡마사)에서 왔습니다. 이리저리 옮겨 다니니 '두서없는'입니다.

senses.en: showing lack of emotional involvement

examples.text: The surgeon spoke in a calm, detached tone, as though describing a problem in engineering.

senses.en: no longer connected or joined

examples.text: a detached part

senses.en: the easing of tensions or strained relations (especially between nations)

examples.text: The two superpowers entered a period of detente that reduced the risk of open conflict.

senses.en: turn away from by persuasion

examples.text: The steep entry fee was enough to deter most casual visitors from attending the exhibition.

senses.en: To prevent something from happening.

examples.text: Heavy fines are intended to deter companies from dumping waste into the river.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēterreō(겁주어 쫓다)에서 왔습니다. 겁을 줘서 하려던 일을 단념시킨다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Something that deters.

examples.text: Along with trial by ordeal, hanging was the most effective deterrent that could be devised in an age without police or prisons.

senses.en: tending to deter

examples.text: the deterrent effects of high prices

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēterrēns(겁주어 막는)에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: Causing damage or harm.

examples.text: Smoking tobacco can be detrimental to your health.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dētrīmentum(손해)에서 왔고 dēterō(닳게 문지르다)가 뿌리입니다. 닳아 없어지는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: To fall outside of, or part from, some norm; to stray.

examples.text: His exhibition of nude paintings deviated from the norm.

senses.en: turn aside; turn away from

examples.text: The pilot deviated from the planned route to avoid a line of thunderstorms.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 dēviāre(길에서 벗어나다)에서 왔습니다. 정해진 길을 벗어난다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: something in an artistic work designed to achieve a particular effect

examples.text: Foreshadowing is a common literary device that hints at events yet to unfold in the story.

senses.en: any clever maneuver

examples.text: he would stoop to any device to win a point

senses.en: an instrumentality invented for a particular purpose

examples.text: a device intended to conserve water

origin.ko: 라틴어 dīvidō(나누다)의 과거분사에서 고대 프랑스어 devis로 이어졌습니다. 계획하고 배치한 것이 '장치, 기법'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: pass on or delegate to another

examples.text: Many legislative powers devolved to the new Scottish parliament in 1999.

senses.en: grow progressively worse

examples.text: A discussion about politics may devolve into a shouting match.

senses.en: be inherited by

examples.text: On the earl's death, the estate devolved upon his nephew, who sold the land within a year.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dēvolvō(굴려 내리다)에서 왔습니다. 책임이 아래로 굴러 내려가는 데서 '이양하다'입니다.
